title: Radius of Curvature Measurements for Osteochondral Allograft Location
author: Zachary Goldstein
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.9nmh5c6
materials: Use area to derive radius of curvature.
Clear all measurements on sagittal slice.
Determining Radius of Curvature of the Capitellum

steps.title: Select Patient and Format Images
steps.instruction: Prepare the CT imaging environment and select a suitable patient for measurement.

substeps.instruction: Obtain CT images tagged 'upper extremity' or 'elbow' and 'lower extremity' or 'knee' from the Department of Radiology.
Exclude patients with prior intra-articular fracture, surgery, degeneration, or variations of normal anatomy.
Randomize the list and select the first patient.
Remove the demographics toggle and set screen format to Series 1:2.
Display axial and sagittal views and set image contrast to 'Bone'.

On the axial image, scroll superiorly from the inferior-most point to identify the axial slice with the longest distance between the anterior and posterior points (APL = Anterior Posterior Length) of the subchondral bone for both medial and lateral condyles.

steps.title: Measure Medial Femoral Condyle Location #1
steps.instruction: Determine the radius of curvature for the first location of the medial femoral condyle.

substeps.instruction: On the sagittal view, scroll laterally from the medial side until the slice aligns with the posterior endpoint of the APL of the medial condyle (if not perfectly aligned, choose the slice medial to the endpoint).
Switch to axial view to ensure the tracked line is visible on the sagittal view, then draw a line on the sagittal view tracing this line.
Measure 15 mm inferior and perpendicular to this line.
Draw a line measuring 10 mm superior from the inferior endpoint of the 15 mm measurement.
Draw two perpendicular lines extending through the condylar bone at the endpoints of the two lines.
Erase all measurement lines on the sagittal slice except for the two perpendicular lines.
Use the 'circle' function to trace a best-fit circle around the radius of the subchondral bone between the two perpendicular lines.
Record the area and perimeter, then use the area to derive the radius of curvature.

steps.title: Measure Medial Femoral Condyle Location #2
steps.instruction: Determine the radius of curvature for the second location of the medial femoral condyle.

substeps.instruction: Clear all measurements on the sagittal slice.
Identify the superior notch of the posterior aspect of the condyle and measure 20 mm down from that point.
Draw a line measuring 10 mm superior from the inferior endpoint of the 20 mm line.
Draw two perpendicular lines at the endpoints of the two measurements through the posterior subchondral bone.
Erase all measurements on the sagittal slice except for the two perpendicular lines.
Draw a circle that best fits the radius of curvature of the subchondral bone between the two perpendicular lines.
Record the area and perimeter, then use the area to derive the radius of curvature.

steps.title: Measure Lateral Femoral Condyle Location #1
steps.instruction: Determine the radius of curvature for the first location of the lateral femoral condyle.

substeps.instruction: On the sagittal view, scroll lateral from the medial side until the slice aligns with the posterior endpoint of the APL measurement line of the lateral condyle (if not perfectly aligned, choose the slice medial to the endpoint).
Switch to axial view to ensure the tracked line is visible on the sagittal view, then draw a line on the sagittal view tracing this line.
Measure 15 mm inferior and perpendicular to this line.
Measure 10 mm superior from the inferior endpoint of the 15 mm measurement.
Draw two perpendicular lines at the endpoints of the two measurements extending through the posterior subchondral bone.
Erase all measurement lines on the sagittal slice except for the perpendicular lines.
Draw a circle that best fits the radius of curvature of the subchondral bone between the two lines.
Record the area and perimeter, then use the area to derive the radius of curvature.

steps.title: Measure Lateral Femoral Condyle Location #2
steps.instruction: Determine the radius of curvature for the second location of the lateral femoral condyle.

substeps.instruction: Clear all lines and measurements on the sagittal slice while remaining on the same slice.
Identify the superior notch of the posterior condyle and measure 20 mm down.
Measure 10 mm superior from the inferior endpoint of the 20 mm line.
Draw two perpendicular lines at the endpoints of the two measurements extending through the subchondral bone.
Erase all measurement lines on the sagittal slice except for the perpendicular lines.
Draw a circle that best fits the radius of curvature of the subchondral bone between the two lines.
Record the area and perimeter, then use the area to derive the radius of curvature.

steps.title: Measure Upper Extremity Radius of Curvature
steps.instruction: Determine the radius of curvature for the upper extremity (elbow) at both 90 and 180 degrees extension.

substeps.instruction: On the coronal image, identify the capitellar articular cartilage bump and draw a 4 mm line medially from that point.
Scroll along the sagittal image until the slice matches the medial edge of the 4 mm line (if not perfect, select the slice medial to the point).
Draw a line through the capitellum bisecting the radial head at the midline.
Draw a line through the capitellum from the superior side approximating the shaft of the humerus (if the arm is angled at 90 degrees, use the anterior aspect of the humerus).
Draw a circle that best fits the radius of curvature of the subchondral bone, using the bisection of the lines as the center.
Record the area and perimeter, then use the area to derive the radius of curvature.
Repeat the entire protocol for 180 degree elbow extension.
